correctness.rationale: The proof normalizes every two-factor composition because a positive word mapping to b has length one, including the possible swap of the intermediate alphabet. Since each factor maps b to b and a to a word containing a, the a-count multiplicativity \(m=cd\) is exact. If the output starts and ends a, nonunit factors have \(c,d\ge2\) and the substituted c-a block forces exactly the repeated interior gaps; conversely the stated equalities construct both factors. Boundary padding handles all \(m\ge2\) with endpoint b and \(m=1\) has an exact additive padding count. The algebraic proof is exhaustive in m, beta, divisors and endpoints. Independent brute searches of all normalized factor pairs for 1013 short words and the enumerative consequences return VERIFY_OK. The finite checks are explicitly not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest full texts arXiv:2603.15177v3, Theorem 1 and Proposition 18, and arXiv:2610.07122v1, Proposition 18, were inspected. Their factor-basis criterion decides instances abstractly; no arithmetic iff on nonnegative interior gaps is given. The printed exclusive-reducibility claim for matrices \(\begin{pmatrix}m&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\) contradicts the verified irreducibility of aba and of \(aba^{m-1}\) for all \(m\ge2\). Published-record semantic searches for fixed-letter morphisms, factorization and periodic gaps found no equivalent claim. Residual older-literature risk is recorded separately; lack of a hit alone was not treated as a novelty proof.
residual_risks: Older word-combinatorics and upper-triangular semigroup literature might encode the periodic-gap criterion in different notation; Honkala 2019 and 2024 were not inspected in full.
A general factor-basis criterion applies to the family, so attribution must distinguish an explicit arithmetic classification from the existence of an abstract decision procedure.
No independent peer review has been performed.

value.rationale: The fixed-generator binary upper-triangular subfamily is natural under semigroup composition and is precisely within a binary structural classification explicitly left unspecified by the motivating paper. The iff replaces arbitrary factor-basis search by divisors of the a-count and equality of integer gaps, corrects a published universal sufficiency assertion using an infinite family with identical matrix parameters, gives an exact prime-count and a nontrivial \(m=4\) census, and proves a generic irreducibility density. These are structural and asymptotic information unavailable from an incidence matrix or a routine substitution of notation; all finite computational aspects are corroborative rather than significance claims.
